subtype: Loving and admiring in adult relationships [Expressing]
passage: Chandrika had to leave for her night shift at the call centre in ten minutes, and the rain had stopped all the autos. She'd planned a proper dinner for Amandeep's birthday, but the day had gone wrong. Instead, she sat on the edge of the bed and wrote on a sticky note: "Dal is in the red box, put it on low. Don't wait up. Saturday, just us, your choice." Amandeep, coming home soaked, read it at the door and grinned. He had wanted her to call, but this was her way: things done, plans made. He made tea, put a note back in her bag that read "Hope the night is quiet", and ran to find her an umbrella.

qa.q: Where was the dal?
qa.a: The dal was in the red box.

qa.q: How did Chandrika show love that evening, and how did Amandeep take it?
qa.a: She showed it through a note, a prepared meal and a plan for Saturday, and Amandeep grinned, understanding it as her way of caring even though he had wanted a call.

qa.q: What could Amandeep do to find out what feels caring to Chandrika?
qa.a: He could ask her what she likes best, whether it is notes, time together or help, rather than assuming.

qa.q: How might Amandeep have felt reading Chandrika's sticky note?
qa.a: Amandeep was likely pleased and touched, as his grin shows, even though he had wanted a call, and he answered with a note of his own.

grounding: Chandrika shows love through help and plans under time pressure, and love styles differ.

subtype: Loving and admiring in adult relationships [Expressing]
passage: Anand admired his lab mentor, Dr. Rao, and had been trying to say so for months. Every Wednesday he stayed after class to ask a question about her methods and took notes as she answered. His girlfriend, Disha, waited in the corridor, scrolling her phone, and said one evening, "You talk about her more than you talk about us." Anand paused. "I don't mean to. Learning from her is how I show I admire someone." Disha nodded slowly. "And I like being taken to dinner, or getting a message at lunch." They stood there, both a little embarrassed. Anand said, "Tell me what feels like care. I don't want to guess." She smiled. "Lunch messages. Start there."

qa.q: On which day did Anand stay after class?
qa.a: He stayed after class every Wednesday.

qa.q: How does Anand show admiration, and what was Disha feeling when she made her remark?
qa.a: He shows it by asking questions and taking notes, and Disha felt somewhat overlooked, though she also seemed willing to talk about it.

qa.q: What could Anand do next to show Disha he cares?
qa.a: He could send her a lunch message and ask what other small things feel like care to her.

qa.q: How might Dr. Rao see Anand's questions?
qa.a: She may see them as interest and respect for her work, though she might not know how much they mean to him.

grounding: Anand shows admiration by learning from a mentor and asks Disha what feels caring.

subtype: Loving and admiring in adult relationships [Expressing]
passage:
"You never say you love me," Sahil said, sitting on the steps outside the library.
Ira looked up from his notes, which she'd been highlighting for him. "What?"
"You text 'ok' and 'reached'. That's it."
"Sahil, I just spent two hours making your revision notes. Yesterday I fixed your cycle. Last week I sat with your Nani at the hospital."
"I know. I noticed. But I need to hear it sometimes."
Ira was quiet. "At home, nobody says it. We just do things."
"At mine, Mummy says it ten times a day."
"So what feels caring to you? Tell me."
He thought. "A message in the day. Just one line. And sometimes, you know, the words."
"And what feels caring to you?" he asked.
"Honestly? When you show up. Like with the cycle."
She handed him the notes. "Okay. One line a day. Even if it feels strange."

qa.q: What did Ira fix for Sahil yesterday?
qa.a: His cycle.

qa.q: What was Sahil feeling when he said Ira never says she loves him?
qa.a: He felt a little hurt and unsure, needing to hear the words even though he noticed all she did.

qa.q: What did Ira and Sahil do that helped?
qa.a: They asked each other what feels caring instead of assuming, and agreed on a small change, one line a day.

qa.q: How does Ira see love?
qa.a: For Ira, love is shown through actions like revision notes, fixing the cycle and sitting with Nani, as in her home where nobody says it.

grounding: Shows young adults expressing love through time, help and messages, and asking each other what feels caring instead of assuming.

subtype: Loving and admiring in adult relationships [Expressing]
passage: Looking back at my first year as a junior engineer, what I remember most is how much I admired Mridul sir. I'm Madhav. He wasn't loud or showy. He just stayed calm when a machine broke and asked everyone what they'd seen before fixing it. I wanted to be like that. So I started watching how he did things. I copied his habit of writing three bullet points before any meeting. I asked if I could shadow him on site visits. Once, after a hard audit, I told him, a bit shyly, "Sir, I've learned more from watching you than from my whole degree." He looked surprised, then smiled and said, "Then ask me more questions. Watching is half." After that I brought him a question every Friday. I think admiration is a kind of love, in a way: you want to grow into what you see in someone.

qa.q: What habit did Madhav copy from Mridul sir?
qa.a: Writing three bullet points before any meeting.

qa.q: How did Madhav feel when telling Mridul sir about learning from him?
qa.a: Madhav felt shy and a little nervous, but full of admiration and respect for the mentor.

qa.q: What did Mridul sir suggest, and why did it help Madhav grow?
qa.a: He suggested asking more questions, because watching is only half, so Madhav brought him a question every Friday.

qa.q: How did Mridul sir react to Madhav's words?
qa.a: He looked surprised and then smiled, suggesting he was touched and pleased.

grounding: Shows a young adult expressing admiration by learning from a mentor and asking what helps, as a form of care.

subtype: Loving and admiring in adult relationships [Expressing]
passage:
Facilitator's note, community centre workshop on friendship and care, Saturday.
Today's pair exercise asked each person to describe how they show care. Mehak and Vandana, best friends for ten years, were sure they knew each other. Mehak said she shows love by planning surprises and sending long voice notes. Vandana said she shows love by remembering small things and turning up with food when someone is ill. Then I asked each to say what makes them feel cared for. Mehak said, "When someone just sits with me, no phones." Vandana said, "Long voice notes, actually. I replay them." They both laughed; each had been giving what she herself liked, not what the other needed most. Mehak admitted she'd felt a little neglected last month when Vandana dropped off soup but didn't stay. They agreed to try the other's way for a month. A good reminder for everyone: people feel cared for in different ways, and it helps to ask.
— Nandita

qa.q: How long have Mehak and Vandana been best friends?
qa.a: For ten years.

qa.q: How had Mehak felt last month when Vandana dropped off soup?
qa.a: She had felt a little neglected, because Vandana didn't stay and sit with her.

qa.q: What did the exercise help Mehak and Vandana do?
qa.a: It helped them ask what makes each feel cared for, and agree to try the other's way for a month.

qa.q: How does Vandana feel about Mehak's long voice notes?
qa.a: She treasures them, replaying them, which shows those notes make her feel cared for.

grounding: Shows young adults learning that love styles differ in close relationships and that asking what feels caring is better than assuming.

subtype: Loving and admiring in adult relationships [Expressing]
passage:
Tuesday
Tonight I asked Amandeep something I should have asked months ago: "What makes you feel most cared for?" I've been sending good-morning messages every day, songs, little hearts, because that's how I feel loved. Amandeep laughed and said, "The messages are sweet. But honestly? When you came and sat with me at the hospital while Papa had his scans, and didn't try to fix anything, that's when I felt it most." I almost didn't go that day; I thought I'd be in the way. Amandeep's way of loving me, I realised, is fixing my cycle chain without being asked and remembering my exam dates. Mine is words. Neither is wrong. We just speak different dialects. We made a small plan: fewer songs, more Sunday walks, and I'll ask before assuming a message is enough. I also thought about Prof. Kulkarni today, and how much I admire the way she listens. Maybe I'll tell her that too.
Deepak

qa.q: Where did Deepak sit with Amandeep?
qa.a: At the hospital while Papa had his scans.

qa.q: How did Deepak feel on learning what made Amandeep feel cared for?
qa.a: Deepak felt surprised and a little humbled, and glad about going to the hospital after almost staying away.

qa.q: What plan did they make?
qa.a: Fewer songs, more Sunday walks, and Deepak asking rather than assuming a message is enough.

qa.q: What makes Amandeep feel most cared for?
qa.a: Quiet presence and time, like being sat with at the hospital without anyone trying to fix things.

grounding: It illustrates a young adult showing love through messages, time and help, and asking a partner what feels caring rather than assuming.
